title: Children and faith
hookLine: teach them diligently, talking on the way (Deuteronomy 6:7)
tomorrow: what did Jesus arrange for his mother at the very end?

lines: A QUESTION FROM THE BACK SEAT.
cards: From the back seat, between a snack and a song: where was I before I was born? Or: does God sleep?
Kids ask the biggest questions at the worst times, at a red light, half-asleep at bedtime, while you're looking for parking. A very old book saw that coming. It doesn't say to wait for a classroom.
It says to talk on the road.

teach.b: Here are the words, from a book Christians and Jews both read: “And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.”
Notice where it starts: in thine heart.
What's passed on is first what's lived. Then the places: the house, the road, bedtime, morning. Ordinary hours.
Faith here gets taught in the cracks of the day more than at a desk.
In the Gospels, when the disciples push children away, Jesus says: “Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.” Suffer here means allow.
And for the back seat, a psalm even answers one of those questions: “Behold, he that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep.”
Here's one to tell a friend: an honest I don't know, said kindly on the way, teaches too. Not everyone has children at home; godparents, aunts, older cousins and neighbors pass faith on as well.

how: Christian families pass on faith in many shapes: bedtime prayers, grace at meals, a Bible story in the car, a question answered honestly; godparents, grandparents and church teachers share the work.

o: passing faith on to children in the ordinary hours of life
a rule that kids must choose a faith by a set age
a church class that teaches children Bible facts

games.q: a seven-year-old asks you at bedtime, "where's heaven?" you're honestly not sure. what fits Deuteronomy 6?
o: make up a confident answer so they feel safe.
say you're not sure, and wonder about it together.
tell them they're too young for that question.
games.why: Deuteronomy puts the talking in ordinary hours, lying down included. what's passed on is what's lived, and an honest I don't know, said kindly, teaches too.

practice: Say Deuteronomy's four times out loud, slowly, one on each breath: sitting, walking, lying down, rising up. On each one, let a face come to mind: a child, a niece, a kid down the street, or the child you once were.

wordCard.voice: Children and faith. Faith passed on in ordinary hours, in the house and on the way, and it starts in the heart.
